To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a thin surface layer of a high oxygen flux material deposited on a MIEC membrane substrate can increase the oxygen transport through the composite membrane.
The oxygen transport through MIEC membranes can be enhanced by adding a thin surface layer that is highly conductive for oxygen transport and has low surface exchange resistance.

the oxygen flux through a dense mixed ionic and electronic conducting membrane can be increased by depositing a thin layer of highly conducting material onto the membrane surface and that the deposition of the layer onto the oxygen-rich side of the membrane is preferable to deposition onto the oxygen-lean side.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a model for the oxygen transport through coated MIEC membranes.
the development of a new generation of oxygen transport membranes (OTM) for efficient oxygen separation.
the oxygen transport through a coated membrane, where the coating is deposited by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and the coating material is a mixed ionic-electron conducting (MIECs) oxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
surface exchange resistance can be a significant barrier for oxygen transport through MIEC composite membrane, and the oxygen flux can be enhanced by reducing the surface exchange resistance.
the addition of a surface layer to a dense MIEC membrane can increase the oxygen flux if the surface exchange coefficient is sufficiently large.
the surface exchange resistance can be reduced by depositing a thin layer of MIES on the surface of the membrane tube.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxygen transport through MIEC membranes may be increased by depositing a layer of a highly conductive MIEC material with a large surface exchange coefficient on the membrane tube.
the oxygen flux through the membrane was enhanced by a factor of ∼ 2 when the surface layer thickness was ∼ 1 µm.
the surface exchange coefficient is the key factor for determining the oxygen transport through a coated membrane and a large surface exchange coefficient can lead to a large oxygen flux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface exchange coefficient and solid/solid inter-facial resistance of the surface coating must be considered in the design of coated composite membranes.
oxygen flux enhancement can be achieved by coating the membrane with a thin, highly conductive, MIEC layer.
oxygen transport through MIEC membranes can be enhanced by depositing an oxygen permeable MIEC surface coating on the substrate.
